summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (LVEF 20%), ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was readmitted for acute decompensated heart failure due to medication non-adherence and increased fluid intake. He presented with chest pain, dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and bilateral lower extremity edema after running out of torsemide and drinking excess water. Treatment included IV furosemide and careful diuresis, which improved his symptoms and reduced his weight from 139.5 kg to 129.2 kg. His kidney function declined during diuresis, with creatinine peaking at 3.0, leading to temporary holding of diuretics. Creatinine improved to 2.4 at discharge. A right heart catheterization confirmed elevated filling pressures. He was discharged home with instructions to hold torsemide for two days, monitor weight, and follow up for lab testing before restarting diuretics.
